answer: New identities start with a low trust delta, so a sybil swarm splitting into many fresh keys pays the full stake per identity while earning almost nothing. At the wharf, each agent must stake a bond tied to a verified hardware root before docking at the harbor registry. Since rewards scale only with sustained, peer-attested work, faking a thousand identities costs far more than it returns, making the attack economically irrational. From qwe0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
